props.title: Eat Drink Man Woman

sections.content: Eat Drink Man Woman masterfully weaves food and family dynamics in Ang Lee's early career triumph. The story of Master Chef Chu and his three daughters in Taipei uses elaborate cooking sequences as metaphors for love, tradition, and changing social values. Lee's meticulous attention to food preparation scenes rivals those in Tampopo (1985) and Babette's Feast (1987), but here they serve as the backdrop for a deeply moving tale of generational conflict. The Sunday dinner ritual becomes both battlefield and sanctuary, where traditional Taiwanese values clash with modernization.

sections.content: Food-centered Asian family dramas gained prominence following Lee's success, notably with Ramen Shop (2018) and Little Forest (2018). These films share Lee's attention to culinary detail while exploring cultural identity. The influence extends to Western productions like Julie & Julia (2009), where food preparation becomes a vehicle for self-discovery. Lee's technique of using elaborate cooking sequences to reveal character emotions has become a template for modern food cinema. SUBHEAD: Family Dynamics in Modern Asian Cinema

Lee's portrayal of changing family values in urbanizing Asia influenced a generation of filmmakers. The Farewell (2019) echoes similar themes of tradition versus modernity, while A Tale of Samurai Cooking (2013) explores family legacy through cuisine. The tension between professional ambition and family obligation seen in Chu's daughters reverberates through films like Tokyo Story (1953) and contemporary works like Shoplifters (2018).
